statement: R2 (owner S68, 2026-10-19). Program link: a value the newer reader typed is linked to a taught measurement by what both are (metric, kind, condition values), never by shared words; the most specific level wins; a candidate that would assume an unstated condition is not preferred; competition between candidates with the same consequences is immaterial (linked to each), otherwise the value stays ambiguous, with the condition axes that would decide; a value no taught measurement measures is reported as outside the teaching. Program evidence: graded evidential force (owner S68): direct, partial contribution, indirect indicator, force not verified, or relevant with its conditions not shown; an outcome is assessed by direct evidence, or by every contributing measurement the teaching lists (at least two), and otherwise only partly. Nothing here authorises a ranking: that also needs the user's need, the conditions of comparison and independent sources. Shadow only.

vocabulary.name: value
vocabulary.meaning: V is a value the newer reader found (a typed quantity).

vocabulary.name: value_kind
vocabulary.meaning: Value V is of quantity kind K (or, when its kind is undecided, K is one of its candidate kinds).

vocabulary.name: value_metric
vocabulary.meaning: Value V is a value of metric X (the quantity knowledge established it).

vocabulary.name: value_condition
vocabulary.meaning: Value V is stated under condition value X of axis A.

vocabulary.name: value_missing
vocabulary.meaning: The quantity knowledge requires axis A for V's metric, and V does not state it.

vocabulary.name: value_product
vocabulary.meaning: Value V is attributed to product P.

vocabulary.name: measurement
vocabulary.meaning: M is a taught measurement of the category.

vocabulary.name: measures
vocabulary.meaning: Taught measurement M measures quantity kind K; L = head (named in the concept's name) or body (only mentioned in its statement).

vocabulary.name: measures_metric
vocabulary.meaning: Taught measurement M measures metric X; L = head or body, as for measures.

vocabulary.name: fixes
vocabulary.meaning: The concept's name fixes condition value X of axis A ("at sleep mode": fan_setting = sleep).

vocabulary.name: requires_axis
vocabulary.meaning: Measurement M needs axis A stated to be interpreted (from its name or its requires_condition relations).

vocabulary.name: leads_to
vocabulary.meaning: A measured_by relation: M bears on outcome O with force F (direct, partial, unverified), per the source verification.

vocabulary.name: indirect_for
vocabulary.meaning: A not_sufficient_for relation: M is only an indirect indicator of outcome O.

vocabulary.name: names_metric
vocabulary.meaning: M names some metric at level L.

vocabulary.name: metric_conflict
vocabulary.meaning: V is a value of a metric that M does not measure, although M names the metrics it measures.

vocabulary.name: head_match
vocabulary.meaning: V matches what M's name says it measures (metric, or kind without a conflicting metric).

vocabulary.name: cand
vocabulary.meaning: M is a candidate measurement for V at level L: metric (same metric, named), kind (same kind, named), mention (same metric, only mentioned).

vocabulary.name: shows_fixed
vocabulary.meaning: V states one of the condition values M fixes on axis A.

vocabulary.name: unshown
vocabulary.meaning: M fixes a condition value that V does not state (linking V to M would assume it).

vocabulary.name: preferred
vocabulary.meaning: M is a candidate for V at level L whose fixed conditions V states.

vocabulary.name: has_pref
vocabulary.meaning: V has a preferred candidate at level L.

vocabulary.name: chosen
vocabulary.meaning: M is among the most specific preferred candidates for V.

vocabulary.name: any_pref
vocabulary.meaning: V has a preferred candidate at some level.

vocabulary.name: assumed
vocabulary.meaning: V has no preferred candidate, and M is a candidate that would assume an unstated condition.

vocabulary.name: rival
vocabulary.meaning: Another chosen candidate competes with M for V.

vocabulary.name: rival_assumed
vocabulary.meaning: Another assumed candidate competes with M for V.

vocabulary.name: linked
vocabulary.meaning: V is linked to M; S = shown (every condition M fixes is stated) or condition_not_shown (the only candidate assumes one).

vocabulary.name: differs
vocabulary.meaning: M1 bears on an outcome, with a force, that M2 does not: linking to one or the other has different consequences.

vocabulary.name: consequential
vocabulary.meaning: V's competing candidates have different consequences.

vocabulary.name: linked_equivalent
vocabulary.meaning: V's competing candidates all have the same consequences; V is linked to each of them (the choice is immaterial for decisions).

vocabulary.name: ambiguous
vocabulary.meaning: M is one of V's competing candidates with different consequences: V is not linked.

vocabulary.name: has_cand
vocabulary.meaning: V has a candidate measurement.

vocabulary.name: no_taught_measurement
vocabulary.meaning: No taught measurement of the category measures what V is: the teaching does not cover it (a knowledge gap, not an error).

vocabulary.name: value_has_axis
vocabulary.meaning: V states some value of axis A.

vocabulary.name: deciding_axis
vocabulary.meaning: A candidate of the ambiguous V fixes axis A and V does not state A: stating it would decide.

vocabulary.name: link_to
vocabulary.meaning: Given to evidence: V is linked to M (linked or linked_equivalent).

vocabulary.name: assumes_condition
vocabulary.meaning: Given to evidence: the link of V to M assumes a condition V does not state.

vocabulary.name: missing_axis
vocabulary.meaning: M needs axis A, and V does not state it.

vocabulary.name: conditions_ok
vocabulary.meaning: Every axis M needs is stated by V, and the link assumes nothing.

vocabulary.name: evidence_force
vocabulary.meaning: Through M, V bears on outcome O with force F: direct, partial, unverified, indirect, or conditions_not_shown (relevant, but cannot assess).

vocabulary.name: bears
vocabulary.meaning: Value V of product P bears on outcome O with force F through M.

vocabulary.name: has_direct
vocabulary.meaning: Some value of P is direct evidence on O.

vocabulary.name: contributes
vocabulary.meaning: A value of P measured by M contributes (partially) to assessing O.

vocabulary.name: has_contribution
vocabulary.meaning: Some value of P contributes to O.

vocabulary.name: two_contributions
vocabulary.meaning: Values of P from two different measurements contribute to O.

vocabulary.name: listed_contribution_missing
vocabulary.meaning: The teaching lists a contributing measurement of O that no value of P supplies.

vocabulary.name: complete_set
vocabulary.meaning: Values of P supply every contributing measurement the teaching lists for O, from at least two measurements.

vocabulary.name: has_indirect
vocabulary.meaning: Some value of P is an indirect indicator of O.

vocabulary.name: outcome_assessment
vocabulary.meaning: What the record allows about product P's outcome O: direct_evidence, all_listed_contributions, partial_contributions, indirect_only, force_not_verified or relevant_conditions_not_shown. Never a ranking by itself: authorisation also needs the user's need, the conditions of comparison and independent sources.

programs.statement: Typed link of values to taught measurements.

rules.statement: A measurement names a metric.
A value of one metric does not belong to a measurement whose name names other metrics only.
Same metric, named by the measurement.
Same kind, named by the measurement, and no conflicting metric.
Candidate at the metric level.
Candidate at the kind level.
Candidate only because the measurement's statement mentions the value's metric (the weakest level).
V states one of the values M fixes on axis A.
Linking would assume a condition the value does not state: M fixes axis A and V states none of the values M fixes on A (several fixed values on one axis are alternatives: "dust and pollen CADR").
A candidate that assumes nothing.
V has a preferred candidate at level L.
The metric level is the most specific.
The kind level, when no metric-level candidate assumes nothing.

rules.rule: chosen(V,M) :- preferred(V,M,mention), not has_pref(V,metric), not has_pref(V,kind).
rules.statement: A mention, only when nothing more specific exists.
V has some preferred candidate.
When every candidate assumes an unstated condition, they are kept as such.
Two chosen candidates compete.
A single chosen candidate is the link.
Two assumed candidates compete.
A single candidate that assumes a condition is a link that cannot assess (the evidence program grades it so).
Two measurements differ in consequence when one bears on an outcome, with a force, that the other does not.
The competition matters for decisions.
The competition matters for decisions (assumed candidates).
Competing candidates with the same consequences: the choice is immaterial; V is linked to each.
As L23, for assumed candidates.
Competing candidates with different consequences: no link.
As L25, for assumed candidates.
V has a candidate.
Closed over the teaching view: no taught measurement measures what V is. The teaching does not cover it; the value is not wrong.
V states axis A.
Stating axis A would tell the candidates apart.

programs.statement: Graded evidential force of linked values, and what it allows per product and outcome.

rules.statement: V states axis A.
A condition the measurement needs is not stated with the value.
A condition the value's own metric requires is not stated.

rules.rule: conditions_ok(V,M) :- link_to(V,M), not missing_axis(V,M,_), not assumes_condition(V,M).
rules.statement: Every needed condition is stated and nothing is assumed.
The value carries the relation's verified force (direct, partial or unverified), bounded to its measurement and conditions.
Relevant to the outcome, but without its conditions it cannot assess it.
The teaching says this measurement is only an indirect indicator of the outcome.
Evidence about product P.
P has direct evidence on O.
A direct measurement of the outcome, under its conditions.
A partial contribution, by measurement.
P has a contribution to O.
Contributions from two different measurements (different quantities, not one value repeated).
Closed over the record: a contributing measurement the teaching lists is not supplied for P.
Every contributing measurement the teaching lists is supplied, from at least two measurements.
The set the teaching lists is present. It assesses O only as far as that list is complete, which the teaching does not prove; independence of sources is not checked here (one document).
Some contributions only: O is partly assessed.
P has an indirect indicator of O.

rules.rule: outcome_assessment(P,O,indirect_only) :- has_indirect(P,O), not has_direct(P,O), not has_contribution(P,O).
rules.statement: Only indirect indicators: never an assessment.
The relation's force was never verified against its source.
Relevant values whose conditions are not stated.
